name: Hodiah
overview: Hodiah is a male figure from the tribe of Levi, uniquely noted as one of two individuals named Hodiah mentioned in the sealed document recorded in Nehemiah 10:1-27, specifically verse 13. His presence on this document highlights his role among the Levites during the post-exilic period. The record in Nehemiah identifies him explicitly, underscoring his significance within the covenant community at that time.
namesAndTitles: The name Hodiah means 'grandeur is YHWH,' reflecting a theophoric element that honors the greatness of God. This proper name is not indicated as being given directly by God but carries a meaning that points to divine majesty, as noted in Nehemiah 10:13.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly identifies Hodiah as a descendant of Levi, linking him to the priestly tribe entrusted with temple duties and worship. Beyond this tribal affiliation, no other family relationships are recorded in the biblical text concerning Hodiah.
scriptureSignificance: Hodiah's mention in the sealed covenant document of Nehemiah 10 signifies his commitment to the renewed covenant community after the Babylonian exile. As a Levite, his inclusion underscores the role of the priestly tribe in upholding the law and worship practices during the restoration of Jerusalem. His presence alongside other leaders in this solemn agreement highlights the communal dedication to God's statutes and the reestablishment of proper worship.
